summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, leg swelling, and elevated creatinine. She had recently been treated for recurrent C. diff and presented with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure and acute kidney injury likely due to poor forward flow. She was managed with IV and then oral furosemide, fluid restriction, and close monitoring. Her heart failure symptoms improved, and kidney function stabilized. The C. diff treatment was completed during admission with no ongoing diarrhea. She remained medically stable for several weeks, but discharge was delayed due to logistical issues. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline diuretic, with follow-up planned for cardiology, nephrology, and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Diabetes with other specified manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, benign, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, hemiplegia affecting unspecified side
